subject.title: Browser-heavy sessions block all main lanes — need dedicated browser lane or per-channel lane routing

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class browser/per-channel lane routing, fold this use case into broader per-agent lane work, or solve it with a scheduler fairness policy that avoids a new lane config surface?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes public scheduler/config semantics and resource-cap behavior across channels and upgrades, which requires maintainer product direction before an implementation PR is safe.

options.title: Design workload lane policy
options.body: Sponsor a bounded scheduler design covering browser/channel/agent classification, aggregate caps, default compatibility, docs, and regression tests before code changes.

options.title: Fold into per-agent lanes
options.body: Treat browser starvation as one use case under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43235 and keep per-channel/browser routing out until per-agent isolation proves insufficient.

options.title: Prefer fairness without lane config
options.body: Avoid new lane configuration for now and pursue foreground reserves, priority aging, or user-work preemption on the shared scheduler.

recommendation.title: Design workload lane policy
recommendation.body: Sponsor a bounded scheduler design covering browser/channel/agent classification, aggregate caps, default compatibility, docs, and regression tests before code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest feature-history signal across the current lane resolver, gateway lane setup, and config/default concurrency surface.
